correctness.rationale: For real Pauli coordinates the norm is |sθ|+‖qθ‖, and the lower-bound gap is 2 Eθ‖sθqθ‖−‖2 Eθ sθqθ‖. Equality is automatic for zero trace. Otherwise rotate the phase to make the trace positive real: equality forces u+v tan θ to lie on one nonnegative ray, so v=0, including the all-zero vector case. At zero trace the integral gives the squared Hilbert–Schmidt norm divided by four. For the upper bound equality forces the continuous angular norm to be constant. A nonzero scalar part has an upward cusp at a zero of sθ that the Euclidean term cannot cancel. With zero scalar part constancy means equal lengths and orthogonality of u,v, precisely square zero by the Pauli product; square zero implies trace zero, including the zero matrix. The checker was inspected, not executed; it corroborates equality examples and inequalities, not the necessity directions. The frozen literature attribution has an incomplete author list and wrong result numbers, separately addressed below.

evidence: With nonzero trace normalized to positive real, a common normer must be the positive-eigenvalue eigenvector of qθ·σ on the positive-scalar semicircle wherever qθ is nonzero. If v≠0, the two ends of that semicircle have opposite limiting qθ directions. Proposition 5 plus the classical M₂ ellipse or the Pauli support formula gives the square-zero equivalence.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: These reductions yield both iff statements, including degenerate cases. The Hilbert–Schmidt identity follows directly because each traceless self-adjoint two-dimensional slice has eigenvalues opposite in sign. No nonroutine independent remainder survives.

evidence: The cited work reduces the lower equality to common norm attainment and the upper equality to angular constancy. Proposition 5 uses the support function of the symmetrized numerical range.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Trace zero makes every Pauli slice a scalar multiple of a self-adjoint unitary or zero. Otherwise the common normer selects the same oriented Pauli ray on the whole positive-scalar semicircle. For the upper criterion a numerical-range ellipse with center a+ib has angular maximum support equal to |a cosθ+b sinθ| plus a seminorm of (cosθ,sinθ); the cusp forces that center to vanish, and constancy then says the ellipse is a disk, so both eigenvalue foci are zero.
